state.label: El Niño Advisory · Approaching Historic
state.detail: El Niño strengthened further through August–September, with SST anomalies exceeding +3.0°C in the eastern equatorial Pacific. CPC (Sep 10) holds a >90% chance of a very strong event this fall–winter and a 75% chance of a historic event (≥+2.5°C on 3-month RONI) during Oct–Dec that would exceed any El Niño since 1950.

narrative: El Niño has intensified into a very strong event that is now approaching historic magnitude. Per the CPC's September 10 discussion, SST anomalies exceeded +3.0°C in the eastern equatorial Pacific; the August monthly Niño indices were +2.52°C (Niño-3.4), +2.5°C (Niño-3) and +3.4°C (Niño-1+2, above +4°C for six straight weeks), while Niño-4 fell to +0.1°C — a strongly east-weighted structure. The weekly Niño 3.4 centred on September 16 reached +3.0°C. Subsurface anomalies remain above +10°C at depth. CPC now carries a 75% chance of a historic event exceeding +2.5°C on the 3-month RONI during Oct–Dec — up from 69% in August — which would surpass every El Niño since 1950, and a >90% chance of a very strong event through fall–winter. IRI's mid-September plume has all 22 models at very strong SON–DJF, many projecting Niño 3.4 above +3.0°C, with El Niño probability 100% through FMA 2027. A positive IOD has now emerged (forecast strongly positive Sep–Dec), the co-occurring mode that historically softens El Niño's monsoon-suppressing effect. The debate is no longer whether or how strong — only whether 2026 sets an outright record.
